title: Near-death experience as a stress test for reality
summary: If consciousness is fundamental, the body is a transceiver and perception is possible without eyes.

body.heading: The brain as a radio
paragraphs: If the universe is a vast interconnected field, individual consciousness is a local whirlpool in that field. When the brain — the localizing mechanism — shuts down, the whirlpool dissolves and returns to the source. The light is not a physical sun but the pure, unconditioned energy of the field itself.
Think of the brain as a radio. When the radio breaks, the music doesn't stop; the radio just can't play it anymore. If the body dies, consciousness is no longer limited to the frequency of the body.

body.heading: Perception without eyes
paragraphs: Seeing is not a mechanical process but an informational one. The field is information — like a hologram, every part contains the whole. With a body, the brain is a filter that restricts the field so you can survive in a 3D environment. Without a body, the filter is removed, and you are immersed in the data of the universe.

Consciousness is not a product of the brain; the brain is a product of consciousness. The body is the screen, the brain the projector, and consciousness the audience. When the screen is destroyed, the audience is still there.

body.heading: The greater self
paragraphs: The 'witness' that remains when the ego dissolves is the pure capacity to observe — the foundation of feeling itself. It is the realization that you are not the whirlpool but the ocean. When a person returns from such an experience they often lose their fear of death, because they have seen that the ocean does not die when the whirlpool disappears.
